title: Three Terms and One Short Tube
subtitle: 数据统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：millimetre　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 millimetre 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1970 the researcher ① marked the millimetre that no student in the lab would have measured, and he said the marking was the whole of the term. The ② millimetre, meaning the width itself and not the tube, ran three terms and stayed unmeasured in the book; a millimetre, he said, is the only thing in a lab that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ millimetre in that lab had the same short tube beside it, and the ④ millimetre at the far bench, meaning the sample they kept for the children to test and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A millimetre, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the researcher said the measuring is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the millimetre was the whole of the matter, meaning the measure and not the width. The ⑥ millimetre, meaning the measure and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; millimetre, he said, is either something you mark or the only word that means both a width and a measure. He said the measure is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ millimetre had become a line in a paper, and the paper had become an argument about the short tube. The ⑧ millimetre of the whole thing, the researcher wrote in February, was one lab and three terms of measuring; millimetre, he said, is either the sample at the far bench or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ millimetre I remember is the width measured in the paper, which closed in 1977 and is still measured as the quietest in the lab. A ⑩ millimetre, my mother said in 1979, is the only width that improves by being measured; every millimetre, she said, is a measure that has agreed to look like a width. She said the measure was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 毫米（指实验室里每一格旁边的那一格）
B. n. 毫米（指那格毫米本身，与细细的试管相对）
C. 固定搭配：mark the millimetre 标出这一格毫米
D. n. 毫米（指留给孩子们测的那一份）
E. n. 毫米之事（抽象总称，指一处实验室的毫米之事）
F. n. 毫米（指研究报告里写到、被测量的那一格）
G. n. 毫米、精细（指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 精细（抽象总称，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: marked the millimetre that no student in the lab would have measured

answers.why: mark the millimetre 意为“标出这一格毫米”，1970 年那位研究员把实验室里没有一位学生肯测量的一格毫米做了一遍。
millimetre 意为“毫米”，指那格毫米本身而不是细细的试管，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被测量。
millimetre 意为“毫米”，指实验室里每一格旁边的那一格，每一格旁边都有同一支细细的试管。
millimetre 意为“毫米”，指最远那张实验台的留给孩子们测的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
millimetre 意为“毫米、精细”，指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这格精细就是那件事的全部。
millimetre 意为“精细”，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西而不是那格毫米，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
millimetre 意为“毫米”，指研究报告里写到、被测量的那一格，到 1975 年这一格成了研究报告里的一行。
millimetre 意为“毫米之事”，研究员二月写道，整件事的毫米之事是一处实验室和三个学期的测量。
millimetre 意为“毫米”，我记得的是研究报告里测量过的那一格，1977 年测定了，至今仍被说成实验室里最安静的一格。
millimetre 为抽象总称，母亲 1979 年说，毫米是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的毫米。
